title: onMount & onCleanup: Owner Scope Root Disposers & Teardowns

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When a room in a hotel is opened, `onMount` turns on the air conditioner and connects the TV. When the guest checks out and the room is locked forever, `onCleanup` turns off the AC and unplugs the TV so nothing wastes electricity. Solid tracks every wire automatically so no cleanup is ever forgotten.
progressiveExplaining.junior: SolidJS has only two primary lifecycle methods: `onMount` and `onCleanup`. `onMount(fn)` runs once after the component's initial DOM nodes have been created and mounted into the document (ideal for DOM measurements or external library initialization). `onCleanup(fn)` registers a teardown function that runs when the current reactive scope (component, effect, or memo) is destroyed or re-evaluated.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Solid replaces complex component lifecycle methods with **Hierarchical Reactive Ownership Scopes** (`Owner`). Every component, `createRoot`, `createEffect`, or `<For>` row creates an `Owner` node with a `.cleanups` array. `onCleanup` simply pushes a disposal callback onto the current active owner's `.cleanups`. When a parent scope is disposed (e.g. an element unmounts), Solid recursively walks the Owner tree and executes all registered cleanups in reverse depth-first order, eliminating memory leaks.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In the runtime, `getOwner()` returns the active `Owner`. `onCleanup(fn)` executes `Owner.cleanups.push(fn)`. When a component unmounts or an effect re-executes, `cleanNode(owner)` is called: it traverses `owner.cleanups`, executing each teardown function synchronously, clears observer dependency sets (`Sources`), and disposes all child `Owners` recursively.

codeComparison.title: React useEffect Multi-Phase Lifecycle vs Solid onMount / onCleanup
codeComparison.summary: React's `useEffect` combines mount, update, and teardown into one hook; Solid separates initial DOM mount from granular disposal scopes.

legacyOrBad.label: React useEffect with Empty Deps
legacyOrBad.snippet: useEffect(() => { const timer = setInterval(...); return () => clearInterval(timer); }, []); // ❌ Re-runs in StrictMode

modernOrGood.label: SolidJS onMount & onCleanup
modernOrGood.snippet: onMount(() => { ... }); onCleanup(() => clearInterval(id)); // ✅ NEW: Clear, deterministic lifecycle

interviewGotchas.question: Can `onCleanup` be used inside a `createEffect` or `createMemo`, or only at the root of a component?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Tests deep understanding of Solid's reactive scope tree.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `onCleanup` **can be called inside any reactive scope**, including inside a `createEffect`, `createMemo`, custom directive, or `<For>` row. When called inside a `createEffect`, the cleanup function executes **every time the effect is about to re-run** (before new execution) as well as when the parent component unmounts.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not assume `onCleanup` only runs on component unmount; when nested inside an effect, it runs on every reactive dependency change before the next run.

interviewGotchas.question: Does `onMount` run on the server during Server-Side Rendering (SSR)?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of isomorphic SSR execution boundaries.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: No. `onMount` **never runs on the server during SSR**. It is strictly a client-side lifecycle hook that executes after the real browser DOM nodes have been created and inserted into the document. Server-side code executes only the synchronous component setup pass.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Placing browser-only code (like `window.localStorage` or `document.querySelector`) outside of `onMount` in the root component body will crash during SSR.
